notes: Glycolysis happens in the mitochondrial matrix and needs oxygen.
other: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm of the cell. It does not need oxygen.

notes: The electron transport chain makes only about 2 ATP per glucose.
other: The electron transport chain and ATP synthase make most of the ATP, about 26 to 28 per glucose.

notes: The Calvin cycle takes place in the thylakoid membranes.
other: The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.

notes: The sodium-potassium pump moves two sodium ions out of the cell and three potassium ions in.
other: The sodium-potassium pump moves three sodium ions out of the cell and two potassium ions in for each ATP.

notes: In a hypertonic solution a cell gains water and may burst.
other: In a hypertonic solution a cell loses water and shrinks.

notes: Newton's second law says acceleration is proportional to mass and inversely proportional to net force.
other: Newton's second law: acceleration is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to the mass.

notes: Momentum is always conserved in a collision, even when external forces act on the system.
other: Momentum of a system is conserved only when the net external force on it is zero.
Yeast fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

notes: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and gains a net 2 ATP.
other: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm. Each glucose gives a net gain of two ATP.

notes: Rubisco fixes carbon dioxide onto RuBP in the Calvin cycle.
other: The enzyme RuBisCO attaches CO2 to ribulose bisphosphate at the start of the Calvin cycle.

notes: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane.
other: Osmosis is the movement of water through a semipermeable membrane toward the side with more solute. Cells in hypotonic solutions swell.

notes: Kinetic energy depends on mass and speed.
other: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity.
